claims.text: The low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi are governed by suppression of a strain-induced phase transformation.
The suppressed transformation would be an fcc-to-nanostructured-hcp transformation during deformation.
A deformation-induced phase transformation would generate obstacles to dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
Failure to generate transformation-related obstacles permits facile dislocation glide, high plasticity, limited work hardening, and low strength in CoCrFeNiTi.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi starts as a single-phase solid solution with a primarily fcc structure.
The proposed test applies tensile or compression deformation at room temperature and a controlled strain rate.
CrCoNi exhibits a magnetically tunable fcc-to-hcp transformation triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation in CrCoNi increases strength without compromising plastic deformation.
Ti in CoCrFeNiTi destabilizes hcp phase energetics.
Ti may suppress the magnetic modulation associated with the fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Deformation of CoCrFeNiTi proceeds mainly by dislocation glide without generating additional strengthening phases.
CoCrFeNiTi will exhibit minimal deformation-induced phase transformation under the specified loading conditions.
CoCrFeNiTi will retain relatively low hardness and yield strength compared with CrCoNi under deformation.
Equimolar CoCrFeNi is expected to undergo a deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation and associated hardening.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to single-phase fcc CoCrFeNiTi-like alloys under room-temperature loading where Ti is the differentiating element controlling phase stability.
In-situ diffraction or high-resolution TEM can be used to compare deformation-induced phase evolution in CoCrFeNiTi and a Ti-free control.
The comparison will measure phase fractions, hardness, yield strength, strain-hardening rate, dislocation density, and microstructural features over the strain path.
Observation of comparable fcc-to-hcp transformation and transformation-associated hardening in CoCrFeNiTi and the Ti-free control would falsify the proposed mechanism.
